title: Section rings across a line comparison with depth-two exceptional image
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-pc-field-extension] and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be flat finite-type morphisms [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $p:Y\to X$ be an $S$-morphism [def-pc-scheme]. Write $X_k=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $X_K=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ for the special and generic fibres, and similarly $Y_K$, with $p_K:Y_K\to X_K$ the induced morphism and $M_K$, $N_K$, $\alpha_K$ the restrictions to the generic fibres [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $Z$ be a finite set of closed points of $X_k$; put $U=X\setminus Z$ and suppose $p^{-1}U\to U$ is an isomorphism. Let $M$ on $X$ and $N$ on $Y$ be invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $\alpha:p^*M\to N$ be a module morphism [def-pc-module-pullback, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] whose restriction to $p^{-1}U$ is an isomorphism. Suppose $\operatorname{depth}\mathcal O_{X,z}\ge2$ for all $z\in Z$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. For each $m\in\mathbf N$, put $$F_m:H^0(X,M^{\otimes m})\longrightarrow H^0(Y,N^{\otimes m}),\qquad s\longmapsto\alpha^{\otimes m}(p^*s),$$ with $F_0$ the ordinary pullback of functions. Every $F_m$ is bijective. If $A_{X,m}\subseteq H^0(X_K,M_K^{\otimes m})$ and $A_{Y,m}\subseteq H^0(Y_K,N_K^{\otimes m})$ denote the images of the restriction maps from $H^0(X,M^{\otimes m})$ and $H^0(Y,N^{\otimes m})$ and $\beta_m$ is the generic-fibre isomorphism induced by $p_K$ and $\alpha_K^{\otimes m}$, then $$\beta_m(A_{X,m})=A_{Y,m}.$$ The maps $F_m$, $\beta_m$ and the two generic restriction maps are additive and $R$-linear, commute with homogeneous tensor multiplication, and send the degree-zero unit to the unit. Thus $\bigoplus_m F_m$ is a graded $R$-algebra isomorphism for the section-ring operations of [def-sc-invertible-section-ring], and the displayed image equalities identify graded $R$-subalgebras. No reducedness, normality, nodality or canonical-bundle hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Fix a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$. The DVR definition makes $R$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$; both total schemes are Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], every nonzero element of $R$ is a unit times a power of $\pi$, so $K=R[1/\pi]$. Consequently the generic fibres are precisely the open loci where $\pi$ is invertible. Since $Z$ lies in the special fibre, $X_K\subset U$ and $Y_K\subset p^{-1}U$. Thus $p_K$ and $\alpha_K$ are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr); morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian). Generic open is the localization at the uniformizer.

proof.text: For every $m\ge0$, set $P_m=M^{\otimes m}$ and $Q_m=N^{\otimes m}$, with $P_0=\mathcal O_X$, $Q_0=\mathcal O_Y$. Iterating [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1) shows that these are invertible. On a trivializing neighbourhood their stalks are free of rank one, so $(P_m)_z\cong\mathcal O_{X,z}$ has depth at least two at each $z\in Z$. Their quasi-coherence and local rank-one presentations give finite type; [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a) gives finite sections on every affine open. All finiteness and boundary-depth hypotheses of Hartogs are now checked for $P_m$.

source.place: Tag 0E9I (lemma-depth-2-hartog), verification of its coherent-module hypothesis for tensor powers of an invertible module.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-depth-two-hartogs-restriction] with $L=X$, $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ and $N=P_m$. Steps 1--2 verify that $X$ is locally Noetherian, that $P_m$ is quasi-coherent with finite affine sections and finite boundary stalks, and that those stalks have depth at least two. The canonical unit $P_m\to j_*(P_m|_U)$ is an isomorphism. Evaluating it on $X$ says exactly that restriction $r_{X,U,m}:\Gamma(X,P_m)\to\Gamma(U,P_m|_U)$ is bijective, including for $m=0$.

source.place: Tag 0E9I (lemma-depth-2-hartog), displayed unit and its global-sections consequence.

proof.text: Multiplication by $\pi$ is injective on every structure stalk of $Y$: at a generic-fibre point it is a unit, and at a special-fibre point the stalk is flat over $R$ by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Tensor the injection $R\xrightarrow{\pi}R$ with that stalk using [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection]. As $Q_m$ is locally free of rank one, multiplication by $\pi$ is injective on its stalks, hence on sections of every open: a section killed by $\pi$ has all germs zero. The same holds for every power $\pi^e$ by induction.

source.place: Flatness preserves the injection defined by a nonzero element of the domain R; local rank-one trivializations transfer the assertion to the line module.

proof.text: The restriction $r_{Y,K,m}:\Gamma(Y,Q_m)\to\Gamma(Y_K,(Q_m)_K)$ is injective. Indeed cover $Y$ by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ trivializing $Q_m$. A section restricting to zero has coefficient $b\in A$ whose restriction on $D(\pi)\subset V$ is zero. The principal-open section formula of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], applied to the free module $A$, identifies this restriction with $b/1\in A[1/\pi]$. By [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], $\pi^e b=0$ for some $e$. Step 4 forces $b=0$. These local zero sections cover $Y$, proving the claim; the argument includes $m=0$ and the empty scheme.

source.place: Tag 01I6, quasi-coherent modules on affines: principal-open sections are localizations; localization equality criterion and the preceding torsion-freeness.

proof.text: Let $\alpha_m:p^*P_m\to Q_m$ be the $m$th tensor power of $\alpha$, using [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2); for $m=0$ use the canonical identity on $\mathcal O_Y$. The map $F_m$ is its map on pulled-back sections. On $p^{-1}U\cong U$, $\alpha_m$ is an isomorphism, so it gives a bijection $c_m:\Gamma(U,P_m|_U)\to\Gamma(p^{-1}U,Q_m|_{p^{-1}U})$. Restriction of the definition of $F_m$ gives $F_m(s)|_{p^{-1}U}=c_m(s|_U)$. Restricting again to $Y_K$ gives the commuting square $r_{Y,K,m}F_m=\beta_m r_{X,K,m}$, where $\beta_m$ is a bijection because both generic maps in step 1 are isomorphisms.

source.place: lemma-tensor-product-pullback; functoriality of pullback and restriction applied to the specified tensor-power map.

proof.text: If $F_m(s)=0$, then step 6 and the injectivity of $c_m$ give $s|_U=0$. The injectivity in step 3 gives $s=0$. For surjectivity take $t\in\Gamma(Y,Q_m)$. Form $v=c_m^{-1}(t|_{p^{-1}U})$ and extend it uniquely by step 3 to $s\in\Gamma(X,P_m)$. Then $F_m(s)-t$ restricts to zero on $p^{-1}U$, hence on $Y_K\subset p^{-1}U$. Step 5 gives $F_m(s)=t$. Thus every $F_m$ is bijective. In the square of step 6, surjectivity of $F_m$ now gives $\beta_m(\operatorname{im}r_{X,K,m})=\operatorname{im}r_{Y,K,m}$, the asserted equality of $A_{X,m}$ and $A_{Y,m}$.

source.place: Agent assembly of Hartogs extension, restriction on the common open, and generic-restriction uniqueness; Tag 0E9I is used through step 3.

proof.text: Pullback of a section is locally $s\mapsto1\otimes s$, followed by the module-linear map $\alpha_m$, so $F_m$ is additive and $R$-linear; the same calculation applies to $\beta_m$ and to restrictions, since $p$ is over $S$. For sections $s,t$ of degrees $i,j$, [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2) sends $p^*(s\otimes t)$ to $p^*s\otimes p^*t$. Applying $\alpha^{\otimes(i+j)}$ applies $\alpha$ to each of the $i+j$ factors, giving exactly $F_i(s)\otimes F_j(t)$. Locally, if $\alpha$ has coefficient $a$, this is the identity $a^{i+j}=a^i a^j$; it holds even where $a$ is not a unit. Restrictions obey the same tensor identity by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Degree zero uses pullback of functions and sends $1$ to $1$. These identities also hold on the generic fibres. By [def-sc-invertible-section-ring], taking the direct sum therefore gives a graded $R$-algebra homomorphism, with inverse given degreewise by the bijections from step 7. Its image equalities respect exactly these products and units and thus identify the stated graded subalgebras.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q55-c2260ca28 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item in full, every cited statement (16 proof_deps and 12 stmt_deps), the parent's step 3 and Stacks 0E9I (divisors.tex l.774). The only changes are proof, proof_deps, proof_origin, searches, status and split_report. There are no new nodes, no SGA, and proof_deps equals the union of uses. The statement is true as stated: p is an isomorphism over U = X minus Z, alpha is an isomorphism on p^-1 U, and Hartogs on X (Z closed points of X_k with depth at least 2) gives injectivity. Flatness of Y (no pi-torsion) gives injectivity of restriction to Y_K, which is contained in p^-1 U, and that gives surjectivity. Properness and reducedness are not needed. Step checks: (1) Noetherian via finite-type-over-Noetherian; K=R[1/pi] via the u*pi^n factorization, so generic fibres are the pi-invertible opens and X_K lies in U. (2) Tensor powers are invertible, with finite affine sections via quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine (a) and depth-2 stalks. (3) The Hartogs node's hypotheses match exactly and its conclusion is the real restriction unit. (4) The flat stalk over R plus flat-tensor-preserves-injection gives no pi-torsion on Q_m. (5) The tilde D(pi) formula b/1 plus localization give pi^e b = 0, so b = 0. (6)-(8) The commuting square, bijectivity, image equality, and multiplicativity via the pullback-tensor formula and a^(i+j)=a^i a^j are correct. Edge cases: Z empty, m=0, empty schemes, nonreduced flat models; dropping flatness of Y gives a counterexample with an extra vertical component. Duplicates: trait-line-section-generic-germs-extension and flat-curve-line-depth need a reduced pure 1-dimensional special fibre, so they do not apply. The declared tool_uses (Hartogs, qc-finite-type-affine, invertible-pullback-tensor, tilde sections) are generic and accepted. Batch-5: lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection is the Mathlib leaf Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap with empty closure, plain flatness algebra outside both assumed statements and their proofs, so the citation stands.
